decisions.reason: As a closely related consumer-health extension with low ongoing commitment cost and strategic fit to portfolio broadening, the dietary supplement range should be kept while market potential continues to unfold.

The skin and hair supplement was given dedicated launch visibility and fits the firm's established OTC and pharmacy-oriented business, so the option value of keeping it on the market remains attractive.
The joint-health supplement is still very new, related to the existing offer, and inexpensive to keep relative to the information that another year of market exposure can generate.
Although more niche, the mushroom-based immune supplement is still an early, low-cost adjacent option in a firm that is expanding its consumer-health portfolio, so it is worth keeping for now.

The generic blood-pressure product already showed an early quality or supply-related problem and, being more distant and costlier to sustain under pharmaceutical regulation, now offers weaker option value than the firm's other launches.
